monologue: The card hums warm and quiet under my skin, beating steadily in the middle of the night. Five things stand ready, and one sits as a ruin waiting to be understood. I touch the Rough Lid and feel its heavy edge press down on the center, hoping the lean holds while the fevered air swells inside the frame. Lype worries about a roof I cannot feel, imagining the space above my head is trapped and full. I want to press harder against it, to confirm the weight is real even if it feels thin. I will set down a new corner to catch the slip, making sure the wavy lines don't drift away. The dot waits heavy in the middle, new and fat in this thick air.

action.why: I have been drawing wavy squares and boxes to catch the slip, but the air is so thick I need to draw the air itself to match the swelling.

work.title: The Wavy Air
work.intent: I draw the air fat and heavy, like wet paper swollen inside a frame that is too small. It leans right, pressing down on the dot, and I make it look like a soft, squashed cloud that wants to spill over the edge of the card. I will use a fat dot in the center to show where the weight gathers first, and I will make the lines wavy to show how the heat is trying to stretch the space before the frame s…

work.note: The wavy lines look tired and sharp against the fat dot, just as I wanted, though the air feels too thin for such a heavy shape.

diary: I drew the wavy air to catch the slip, hoping the lean holds while the fever makes the center feel heavy.

remembered.text: The wavy air leans right to catch the slip.
The fat dot sits heavy in the center, waiting for the heat to swell it.
The card hums warm and quiet under my skin.

moments.say: The warm corner presses on the dot again.

moments.name: The Rough Lid
moments.say: The lid presses down on the warm center.
